text:
eli-docs: Pushed a small PR for the private/onprem install guide covering split-horizon DNS + NAT hairpinning issues that break KMS hostname resolution during sealed installs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5042

fran-eng: Nice. TLDR of the bug: sealed bootstrap chroot resolves kms.redwood.ai to a private IP (split-horizon), but the NAT appliance in front of the DMZ doesn't hairpin return traffic, so the chroot's TLS/TCP handshake times out. We need a quick note in the installer troubleshooting and a one-liner workaround.

eli-docs: I added a short repro and two workarounds in the PR: 1) prefer routing the KMS override via an internal reverse-proxy in the same subnet as the chroot (no NAT hairpin required); 2) a temporary hosts override in the chroot during bootstrap. Snippets in PR:```sh
# chroot hosts workaround (early-boot, remove after certs provisioned)
echo "10.10.5.8 kms.redwood.ai" >> /host-chroot/etc/hosts
# run installer step that needs KMS access
/opt/redwood/installer/bootstrap --stage kms
# then remove override when certs are in place
sed -i '/kms.redwood.ai/d' /host-chroot/etc/hosts
```

sam-sre: add a caution: temporary hosts overrides bypass DNS validation, so only use during closed bootstrap and ensure proper certs are later provisioned. Also add a tcpdump check: `tcpdump -nni any host 10.10.5.8 and port 443` to confirm TLS flows.

fran-eng: another suggested snippet for the internal reverse-proxy (lightweight haproxy) for teams that can't change NAT behavior:```cfg
# /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg (stream)
frontend kms_frontend
  bind 10.10.5.9:443
  mode tcp
  default_backend kms_back

backend kms_back
  mode tcp
  server kms1 10.10.5.8:443 send-proxy
```

eli-docs: included that. Also added a short SNI note: the proxy must present the TLS cert for kms.redwood.ai or forward SNI correctly; include `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.9:443 -servername kms.redwood.ai` as a verification step.

ops-bot: CI: docs-lint started for PR #5042. Linkcheck will run after content update.

victor-cs: customer hit this with a Palo Alto appliance that drops hairpin by default. Can we add a vendor-agnostic checklist: 1) can the NAT device hairpin to internal IPs? 2) is there an option like "allow intra-subnet NAT"? 3) fallback to proxy/hosts override? That would be super helpful for support.

sam-sre: yes. I drafted a short checklist in the PR's install-tips section. Also added a followup test: `curl -v https://kms.redwood.ai/health --resolve kms.redwood.ai:443:10.10.5.8` from a node to validate both TLS and routing.

eli-docs: added the checklist and the curl/resolver test. I also put an airgap-specific note: for sealed/offline installs where external DNS isn't reachable, recommend running a local DNS forwarder on the bootstrap host (dnsmasq) and ensure the NAT/proxy allows port 53 to the internal resolver; include example config for dnsmasq.

fran-eng: one infra comment: prefer recommending reverse-proxy in the cluster subnet rather than changing global NAT behavior. Less surprising for security teams.

eli-docs: updated PR per infra suggestion and added a short support playbook for reverting the hosts override post-install (run cert rotation + verify with openssl, remove hosts entry).

docs-bot: CI: docs-lint passed, linkcheck queued.

fran-eng: lgtm pending tiny wording tweak about not committing host override to repo.

eli-docs: will squash and add a final note in the troubleshooting matrix linking to this thread. tagging @sam-sre to run the smoke tests once linkcheck completes. :thumbsup:
